questions.body: SAMPLE: What does a red octagonal sign usually mean?
questions.explanation: SAMPLE: A red octagon is the usual stop sign.

questions.body: SAMPLE: What does an upside-down triangle with a red border usually mean?
questions.explanation: SAMPLE: An inverted triangle usually means give way.

questions.body: SAMPLE: Which shapes are commonly used for warning signs?
questions.explanation: SAMPLE: Warning signs are often triangles or diamonds.

questions.body: SAMPLE: A blue circular sign usually gives what kind of instruction?
questions.explanation: SAMPLE: Blue circles usually give mandatory instructions.

questions.body: SAMPLE: At an unmarked junction, who usually has priority in a right-hand traffic country?
questions.explanation: SAMPLE: Many right-hand traffic countries use priority to the right.

questions.body: SAMPLE: When may you overtake on the inside lane of a motorway?
questions.explanation: SAMPLE: Overtaking on the inside is generally not allowed.

questions.body: SAMPLE: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches?
answers: Stop in the middle of the road
questions.explanation: SAMPLE: Make room safely and let it pass.

questions.body: SAMPLE: Which documents should you usually carry while driving?
questions.explanation: SAMPLE: Carry your licence and the vehicle papers.

questions.body: SAMPLE: A traffic light shows amber after green. What should you do?
answers: Stop if you can do so safely
questions.explanation: SAMPLE: Amber means stop unless stopping would be unsafe.

questions.body: SAMPLE: How does wet weather affect stopping distance?
questions.explanation: SAMPLE: Stopping distances grow on wet roads.

questions.body: SAMPLE: Who must wear a seat belt in a car?
questions.explanation: SAMPLE: Everyone must wear a seat belt.

questions.body: SAMPLE: What is a safe reaction when you feel tired on a long drive?
answers: Open the window and keep going
questions.explanation: SAMPLE: Stop and rest when you feel tired.
